p: Sardis: Sardis is the name of a most flourishing and famous city, where the kings of Lydia kept their courts.
write: The fifth passage is to the pastors of Sardis. The introduction is taken from Re 1:4,16.
name that thou livest: You are said to live, but are dead indeed.
ready to die: Other things, whose state is such, that they are now going, and unless they are confirmed, will perish without delay.
which have not defiled their garments: That is, who have with all religion guarded themselves from sin and moral corruption, even from the very show of evil; Jude 1:23.
white: Pure from all spot, and shining with glory. So it is to be understood always hereafter, as in Re 3:5.

worthy: They are suitable and proper, that is, because they are justified in Christ, as they have truly showed it: for he who acts righteously is righteous in the same way that a tree bears good fruit; Ro 8:18.
And to the angel of the: The sixth passage is to the pastors of Philadelphia. The introduction is taken from Re 1:18.
key of David: All power of rule in commanding and forbidding, in delivering and punishing. The house of David is the Church, and the continual promise of David's kingdom belongs to Christ.
I know thy works: The note of praise is in this verse of promises, and Re 3:9 to bring home again them that wander, in Re 3:10 to preserve the godly and in Re 3:11 to exhort.
of the synagogue of Satan: I will bring them to that case.

and worship before thy feet: That is, fall down and worship either you civilly, or Christ religiously at thy feet (this is how I would rather take it) whether here in the Church (which seems more proper to the argument here) or there in the world to come, for Christ shall truly fulfil his word.
kept the word of my patience: Because you have been patient and constant, as I would have my servants be.
Him that overcometh will I make: The conclusion which contains a promise, and a commandment.
and I will write upon him: That is, the new man shall be called after his father, mother, and his head Christ.
And unto the angel of the: The seventh passage is to the pastors of the Church of Laodicea. The introduction is taken out of Re 1:5.
Amen: Amen sounds as much in the Hebrew tongue, as truly, or truth itself.
beginning of the creation of God: Of who all things that are made, have their beginning.

I know thy works: The proposition of reproof is in this verse, and in Re 3:16 a threat while in Re 3:17 a confirmation declares the same. To faith and repentance in Re 3:18,19 a conditional promise is added in Re 3:20.
and poor: The spiritual misery of men is metaphorically expressed in three points which are matched as corresponds to those remedies offered in Re 3:18.
zealous therefore: Zeal is set against those who are neither hot nor cold.
if any man hear my voice: This must be taken after the manner of an allegory; Joh 14:23.
To him that overcometh will I: The conclusion, consisting of a promise, as in Re 2:26 and of an exhortation.
